subject: Immediate: APAC edge disruption — recommended traffic shift and verification steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@faststore.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T07:12:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate: APAC edge disruption — recommended traffic shift and verification steps

Elaine / FastStore Ops team,

Quick update and immediate guidance — we are observing elevated error rates and streaming disconnects from our APAC edge (ap-southeast-1 region) starting ~2028-09-18T06:40Z. Root cause analysis is ongoing (engineering is investigating an upstream peering saturation event).

Impact:
- A subset of long-lived streaming sessions and realtime token ingestion are timing out or receiving 5xxs.
- Automated fallback to EU is in effect for new sessions, but some client-side connections remain pinned to APAC and are seeing higher latency.

Immediate customer actions (recommended, quick to apply):
1) Switch live traffic to our EU endpoint for the short term. You can set the header: "X-Redwood-Region: eu-central-1" or target the EU endpoint: https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?region=eu.
2) If you use client-side SDKs, toggle the fallback flag: fallback_region=eu in your runtime config and restart workers. This is non-disruptive for new connections.
3) For streaming connections, reconnect clients after applying the header — session continuation across regions is not supported; warm caches will repopulate in ~30s.

We attached a short checklist (apac-evacuation-checklist.pdf) and a script with curl examples (kb-traffic-shift-script.sh) to speed this.

We will notify you when APAC is cleared. In parallel, Dylan is preparing a safe cutover script and notes about KV-cache considerations for any model with long context.

If you prefer, we can schedule a five-minute screen-share with engineering now — I can join Ops and Dylan. Please confirm whether you will switch to EU now or want Redwood to initiate a controlled redirect for you.

Apologies for the interruption.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: apac-evacuation-checklist.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@faststore.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-18T08:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: APAC edge disruption — recommended traffic shift and verification steps

On Mon, Sep 18, 2028 at 07:12 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick update and immediate guidance — we are observing elevated error rates and streaming disconnects from our APAC edge (ap-southeast-1 region)...

Elaine — short answers: auth keys and tokens remain valid across regions (no key rotation required). The only change is the regional endpoint header or query param.

Technical notes and safe cutover steps (tested):
A) For REST generation:
- Example curl to EU endpoint (preserves same token):
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-central-1" \
    https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","prompt":"hello"}'

B) For streaming clients (websocket):
- Close existing WS connections to APAC, open new WS to wss://stream.api.redwood.com/?region=eu-central-1
- If you use our official SDK, set config.region = 'eu-central-1' and call client.reconnectAll()

C) KV/cache considerations:
- Any in-memory KV cache bound to APAC instances will not be replicated. Expect a short warm-up period for repeated prompts; avoid bulk cold-start traffic for 5–10 minutes.

D) Rollback:
- To revert, change header to X-Redwood-Region: ap-southeast-1. We will signal when APAC is fully healthy.

Attached is a small shell script (kb-traffic-shift-script.sh) that runs a health-check loop and updates a header on your fleet via our sample patch endpoint. Please run in a maintenance window if you have rolling restarts.

I'll stand by on the Zoom link if you want live help. ETA for clearance: engineering estimates 90–180 minutes for peering restoration, subject to downstream carrier fixes.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kb-traffic-shift-script.sh

Thanks everyone — quick summary and next steps:

Customer decision: FastStore confirmed switching new traffic to EU at 08:05Z and reconnecting streaming clients. They saw immediate improvement for new sessions.

Work completed by Redwood:
- At 08:02Z Dylan validated EU endpoint auth and shared the shift script.
- At 08:06Z we confirmed reconnects to EU succeeded and error rates dropped for new sessions.
- Engineering continues to investigate peering saturation and will publish RCA within 72 hours.

Action items / owners:
- Dylan: prepare full technical RCA draft and timeline (ETA: 2028-09-20T17:00Z).
- Vanessa: open the incident credit ticket and notify billing (ETA: today EOD).
- Karthik: follow up with FastStore AE on contract/credits and note in HubSpot (deal HS-4321).
- Tessa: schedule post-incident customer call once RCA draft is available and share shortened incident log bundle via Drive.

Please confirm when you've completed the redeploy on your side so we can mark the customer action item closed. We'll also attach the final logs and the formal postmortem to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_example_doc/evac-playbook

Apologies again for the disruption — we'll be in touch with the RCA and mitigations to reduce risk of recurrence (additional regional peering health checks and automated proactive routing).

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
